output_json.patch_notes: Root-cause fix: added `AbstractResourceHandler.isPathUnderBase(basePath, resourcePath)`, a static helper that normalizes both the configured base resource and the fully-resolved request path with `StringUtils.cleanPath` (the same normalizer the resource sink uses) and confirms the resolved path is the base itself or a true descendant (prefix match on a slash boundary, not a naive substring check). `ExternalResourceHandler.getResource(String)` and `ClassPathResourceHandler.getResource(String)` now: (1) return null immediately if `UriPath.canonical()` rejects the path (previously a null canonical path was silently treated as "no suffix", falling back to serving the base directory/welcome file); (2) call `isPathUnderBase(baseResource, addedPath)` after computing the combined path and before constructing `ExternalResource`/`ClassPathResource`, returning null if the check fails. Added regression tests exercising the real (non-mocked) resource stack: a Windows-separator traversal payload (`/foo\..\..\<target>`) that `UriPath.canonical()` does not treat as ".." but `StringUtils.cleanPath()` does resolve, verifying it is now rejected for both handlers, plus a happy-path test confirming legitimate in-bounds requests still resolve. Full existing suite (295 tests) passes unchanged.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk: the new check reuses the exact normalization (`StringUtils.cleanPath`) already used internally by `ExternalResource`/`ClassPathResource`, so it should not reject any path that would have resolved to a location inside the configured root; it only rejects paths whose sink-normalized form falls outside the base. All 295 existing unit/integration tests (including PowerMock-heavy resource-handler tests that mock the ExternalResource/ClassPathResource constructors) pass unmodified, since the new check runs purely on plain strings before those objects are constructed. `JarResourceHandler` was intentionally left unchanged — it resolves resources via `Class.getResourceAsStream` confined to the running jar's own classpath entries (no `java.io.File`/`cleanPath` sink), so it isn't part of this CWE-022 sink family and wasn't referenced in the alert traces. Builds and full test suite were verified inside the project's Docker container using the provided wrapper.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal in Spark's static-resource handlers (ExternalResourceHandler and ClassPathResourceHandler). The request path was canonicalized with UriPath.canonical(), which only recognizes '/'-delimited ".." segments and lets other separators (e.g. Windows-style backslashes) pass through untouched. The resulting path was then concatenated with the configured base resource and handed to ExternalResource/ClassPathResource, whose constructors call StringUtils.cleanPath() — a *different*, more permissive normalizer that does convert backslashes to '/' and resolves ".." sequences (silently retaining any that can't be canceled, e.g. producing "/../etc/passwd" or escaping into a sibling directory) instead of rejecting them. The mismatch between the two normalizers let a crafted request path escape the configured static-file root. Added a shared containment check (`AbstractResourceHandler.isPathUnderBase`) that re-normalizes the base and the fully resolved path with the exact same `StringUtils.cleanPath()` the sink uses, and rejects the request (returns null, i.e. 404) unless the resolved path is the base directory itself or a genuine descendant of it. This is applied at the shared root cause in both handlers, right before resource construction, covering both the file-system and classpath resource flows named in the alert as well as same-class bypass variants (alternate separators/encodings) since the check operates on the final normalized path rather than trying to enumerate every bypass pattern.
